newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: $1 million note worthless, U.S. warns Malaysians.
newsitem.headline: $1 million note worthless, U.S. warns Malaysians.

text.p: The United States has no $1 million notes in print, and Malaysians should not be fooled into thinking otherwise, a U.S. diplomat warned on Thursday.

"The $1 million is absolutely worthless. It is not real and I don't want to see any Malaysian getting conned," U.S. embassy regional security officer James Ferguson was quoted as saying by the national Bernama news agency.
Ferguson said he received a fake $1 million bill with a purported certificate of authenticity from a Malaysian about two weeks ago.
According to the certificate, the bill was a limited edition produced by the "American Bank Note Company" in 1988 for the "International Association of Millionaires", Bernama said.
The certificate also carried signatures of a Tari Steward as IAM international treasurer and C.W.Aurand Jr as American Bank Note Co president, the agency said.
Ferguson said no such limited edition of the American currency has been issued by the U.S. Treasury and that the highest denomination for the U.S. currency remains the $100 note.
The fake bill has been handed to the Malaysian police, who are investigating, Bernama reported.
